issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor, getters, setters and other methods use camelCase names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This creates an inconsistency within the solution repository: the declared fields do not match the names used throughout the class, which will cause compilation errors and confuse students comparing the solution to the UML and the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent with the UML and the rest of the class. Rename the declared fields to use camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or alternatively update all usages to match the declared snake_case names. Ensure constructor assignments and all getters/setters reference the same field names so the class compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The solution implementation declares the Lecture attributes using snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the problem statement and the rest of the implementation (constructor parameters, getters/setters, toString, and method bodies) use camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This mismatch creates a mapping/confusion for students and will cause compilation errors or unexpected behavior because the declared field names do not match the names referenced elsewhere.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent camelCase attribute names across all artifacts. In solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java rename the private fields to: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors so they match the UML, constructor, getters/setters and other method references (or alternatively rename all references to use the snake_case fields, but prefer camelCase to match Java conventions and the problem statement).
